### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A31, A22, A20, A23, A24, A26, A25 and A32 ran as one fixed chain (A31→A22→A20→A23→A24→A26→A25→A32): each source sent almost all of its outgoing transitions to a single successor (A23→A24 in 100 in 100, A24→A26 and A26→A25 in about 99 in 100, A25→A32 in about 93 in 100), and every monitored pair co-occurred in all traces with one fixed order and one fixed gap (for example A20 always two steps before A24, A26 always one step before A25). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG002, LAG017, LAG022]
- In the later window this chain is broken up: A23 now leads directly to A32 in about 49 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (not observed earlier), while A23→A24 fell from all cases to about 15 in 100; A31 enters directly at A24 in about 47 in 100 (not observed earlier), while A31→A22 fell to about 52 in 100; A20 and A22 also gained direct transitions into A24, A25 and A26 (roughly 6–27 in 100), so A22→A20 fell from about 99 to 56 in 100 and A20→A23 from about 99 to 67 in 100. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR007]
- The later window also shows new backward transitions from the second block to the first: A24 now goes to A22 in about 23 in 100 and to A20 in about 11 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A25 goes to A20, A23 and A22 (about 20, 20 and 12 in 100) instead of mostly to A32 (down from about 93 to 42 in 100), and A26 goes to A20, A22 and A23 (about 13, 12 and 9 in 100) in addition to A25. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG014, LAG015, LAG019, LAG021]
- The order between the two blocks reversed or lost its fixed direction: earlier A20, A22 and A23 preceded A24, A25 and A26 in 98–99 in 100 traces; in the later window A24 precedes A23 in about 84 in 100 (previously about 0), A24 precedes A20 in about 73 in 100, and pairs such as A20–A26 and A23–A25 now occur in both orders in roughly equal shares, with little interleaving in either window (at most about 2 in 100). All pairs still co-occur in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Formerly fixed distances spread and some old forward orders became rare: A22→A23, always two steps apart earlier, now ranges over two to five steps; A20 followed by A24 within five steps occurs in only about 52 of 200 later traces (200 of 200 earlier); and pairs almost unobserved earlier, such as A24 before A20 (about 148 of 200 traces) or A24 before A22 (about 94 of 200), now appear regularly. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG007, LAG016]
- Relative positions moved consistently with this reordering: A20, A22 and A23 occur later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.59, 0.56 and 0.62 earlier versus 0.63, 0.59 and 0.68 later), while A24, A25 and A26 occur earlier (about 0.65, 0.70 and 0.67 versus 0.59, 0.68 and 0.64). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the ordering constraints between the two activity blocks changed: in the earlier window A20, A22 and A23 always executed before A24, A25 and A26 within the fixed chain A31→A22→A20→A23→A24→A26→A25→A32, whereas in the later window this sequence is loosened and partly inverted — A24, A25 and A26 frequently run before A20, A22 and A23, A23 often bypasses A24–A26 by leading directly to A32, A31 sometimes enters directly at A24, and new backward transitions (A24→A22/A20, A25→A20/A23/A22, A26→A20/A22/A23) create detours back through the earlier activities. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL003, REL006, REL007, LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG027]

The change is shown directly rather than inferred from marginals: relational items record the order reversal itself (A23 before A24 fell from about 99 to 15 in 100 traces while the reverse rose from 0 to about 84 in 100), the successor profiles record the new and weakened edges, the lag distributions record both the new relations and the spread of formerly fixed gaps, and the position shifts agree in direction. The volume of qualifying evidence also far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 49 control-flow items qualified where about 0.47 would be expected by chance, and every item's difference exceeds those of about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits. [REL006, DIR003, DIR007, LAG013, LAG027, POS003, POS004]

Limitations: all items come from a single control-flow family and many describe the same underlying restructuring from different angles, so they are consistent but not independent confirmations; and the evidence cannot distinguish a uniform loosening of the sequence across all cases from a mixture in which only part of the later traces follow a new reversed or bypassing variant while the rest keep the old chain — the near 50/50 pair orders for A20–A26 and A23–A25 fit both readings. [REL003, REL004, REL007]

Other differences: none — every qualifying item involves the same six activities (with A31 and A32 as entry and exit) and their mutual order.
